messages.subject: INLA Spatial-Temporal Help!
parts:
I am generating predicted values XY, and Prediction. My model keeps getting this error. I'd like to save the predicted values to each geospatial location, but I'm getting this unknow error.


# YOU ARE HERE, THIS IS THE CLOSEST WORKING CODE PAST THE PREDICTION STACK

# ------------ - ------------------- --------------------- ----------------

# Define the coordinates of the observation locations
locations <- cbind(data$longitude, data$latitude)

# Create a mesh for spatial prediction
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(
  loc = locations,
  max.edge = c(0.1, 0.5),  # Adjust the edge lengths as needed
  cutoff = 0.01,  # Minimum allowed distance between points
  offset = c(0.1, 0.5)  # Adjust these values as needed
)

# Visualize the mesh
plot(mesh, main = "Spatial Mesh")
points(locations, col = "red", pch = 16, cex = 0.5)

spde_model <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  alpha = 2,
  prior.range = c(10000, 0.01),  # P(range < 10000) = 0.01
  prior.sigma = c(3, 0.01)       # P(sigma > 3) = 0.01
)

# Create the index set for the SPDE model
s_index <- inla.spde.make.index(
  name = "spatial.field",
  n.spde = spde_model$n.spde,
  n.group = length(unique(conflict_data$time_index))
)



extended_data$log_fat <- log(extended_data$fat + 1)

# Create the spatial field index
index_spde <- inla.spde.make.index(name = "spatial.field", n.spde = spde$n.spde)

# Create the stack for the observed data
stack_obs <- inla.stack(
  data = list(y = extended_data$log_fat[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)]),
  A = list(1, inla.spde.make.A(mesh = spde$mesh, loc = cbind(extended_data$longitude[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)], extended_data$latitude[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)]))),
  effects = list(
    data.frame(intercept = 1,
               time_index = extended_data$time_index[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               ID = data$event_id_n[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               X1 = data$X1[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               X2 = data$X2[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               X3 = data$X3[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               popT_Ev = data$popT_Ev[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               b0 = data$b0[!is.na(extended_data$log_fat)]
              ),
    index_spde
  )
)
print("Stack_Obs created")

# Create a grid of locations for prediction
x.res <- 100  # Number of grid points in x direction
y.res <- 100  # Number of grid points in y direction

Seq.X.grid <- seq(from = min(data$longitude), to = max(data$longitude), length = x.res)
Seq.Y.grid <- seq(from = min(data$latitude), to = max(data$latitude), length = y.res)

pred.grid <- as.matrix(expand.grid(x = Seq.X.grid, y = Seq.Y.grid))
print("Prediction Grid Created")

# Create the stack for the prediction data
stack_pred <- inla.stack(
  data = list(y = NA),
  A = list(1, inla.spde.make.A(mesh = spde$mesh, loc = cbind(extended_data$longitude[is.na(extended_data$log_fat)], extended_data$latitude[is.na(extended_data$log_fat)]))),
  effects = list(
    data.frame(intercept = 1,
               time_index = extended_data$time_index[is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               ID = data$event_id_n[is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               X1 = data$X1[is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               X2 = data$X2[is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               X3 = data$X3[is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               popT_Ev = conflict_data$popT_Ev[is.na(extended_data$log_fat)],
               b0 = conflict_data$b0[is.na(extended_data$log_fat)]
              ),
    index_spde
  ),
  tag = 'pred'
)
print("Stack_Pred created")

# Combine estimation and prediction stacks
stack <- inla.stack(stack_obs, stack_pred)
print("Stack combined")

# Define the formula
unique_ids <- unique(conflict_data$event_id_n)

formula <- as.formula(paste0("y ~ -1 + intercept + ",
                        paste0(colnames(conflict_data[, c("X1", "X2", "X3", "popT_Ev", "b0")]), collapse = " + "),
                        " +  f(ID, model = 'iid') +  f(spatial.field, model = spde,
                        group = spatial.field.group, control.group = list(model = 'ar1'))"))

# Fit the model
result <- inla(
  formula,
  data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde = spde),
  family = "nbinomial",
  control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack), compute = TRUE),
  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE),
  verbose = TRUE
)
print("Model Fitted Result created")

# Extract predictions
index_pred <- inla.stack.index(stack, "pred")$data

#index_pred <- inla.stack.index(stack_join, "Pred")$data
post_mean_pred <- result$summary.linear.predictor[index_pred, "mean"]

proj_grid <- inla.mesh.projector(
  mesh,
  xlim = range(pred.grid[,1]),
  ylim = range(pred.grid[,2]),
  dims = c(x.res, y.res)
)

post_mean_pred_grid <- inla.mesh.project(proj_grid, post_mean_pred)

# Normalize the predicted values
predmean <- post_mean_pred_grid / max(post_mean_pred_grid)

# Plot the predicted fat for 2023
plot_data <- expand.grid(X = Seq.X.grid, Y = Seq.Y.grid)
plot_data$predicted_fat <- as.vector(predmean)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = predicted_fat)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Predicted Fat", x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")


save_predictions <- function(year, data, mesh, result, index_pred) {
  # Extract the predictions for the given year
  predictions <- result$summary.fitted.values$mean[index_pred]
 
  # Create a data frame with the predictions and spatial coordinates
  prediction_df <- data.frame(
    longitude = data$longitude,
    latitude = data$latitude,
    predicted_fat = predictions
  )
 
  # Remove any rows with NA predictions (if any)
  prediction_df <- na.omit(prediction_df)
 
  # Save to CSV
  file_name <- paste0("predicted_fat_", year, ".csv")
  write.csv(prediction_df, file = file_name, row.names = FALSE)
 
  cat("Predictions for", year, "saved to", file_name, "\n")
}


#

The error that is this:
[1] "Stack_Obs created" [1] "Prediction Grid Created" [1] "Stack_Pred created" [1] "Stack combined" Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully. If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>. *** inla.core.safe: inla.program has crashed: rerun to get better initial values. try=1/1 Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : The inla-program exited with an error.
